concerns.text: Task T005.1 mandates generating 'human_verified_label' fields via a 'lightweight rule-based solver or heuristic' if the external dataset is missing. This violates SC-006 and the Spec's Assumption about measurement validity, which require the metric to be measured against *human-verified* labels. A heuristic-generated label is synthetic, not human-verified, effectively weakening the validation requirement to a self-fulfilling prophecy.

Task T008 mandates loading 'mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B' as a proxy for a '1B parameter MoE' student. The Mixtral-8x7B model is ~47GB in full precision and exceeds 7GB RAM even with int8 quantization. This task is physically impossible under FR-007 (≤7GB RAM) and contradicts the Spec's Assumption that a 1B model fits. The task weakens the hardware constraint by proposing an unexecutable model.

Task T032 introduces a hard halt condition for 'log-probability variance < 1e-9' for SSM compatibility. The Spec's Edge Case 3 only requires halting if 'output dimension mismatch > 0'. The variance threshold is an undocumented, arbitrary constraint not found in the Spec, introducing a silent narrowing of the acceptance criteria that could cause false positives in valid SSM runs.

Task T045 cites 'Liang & Zeger (1986)' as the primary reference for cluster-robust standard errors in a small-N (n=5) experimental design. The Spec (FR-006) requires a t-test or Wilcoxon test with Bonferroni correction. This citation appears to be a hallucination or misapplication for the specific design, violating the Constitution's 'Verified Accuracy' principle and weakening the statistical rigor required by FR-006.

Task T002 mandates installing 'torch' with '--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu' to enforce CPU-only. While this aligns with FR-007, the task description tags it as '(FR-007)'. FR-007 is about memory/time constraints, not dependency installation. More critically, if the CPU wheel fails to install or is incompatible with the runner's OS, the task fails silently or falls back to GPU (if available), weakening the 'CPU-only' constraint unless the task explicitly mandates a hard failure on non-CPU installation.
